records.failureSummary: Implemented the DATA_DIR persistence store, atomic writes, mutation mutex and signing-secret store, and wired them into the server initialize hook. New src/store/persistence.js: mkdirSync(DATA_DIR, recursive) + load users.json into memory (before listen), records are whitelisted to exactly {id, username, normalizedUsername, passwordHash, salt, kdfParams, createdAt} so an extra caller-supplied password field is dropped and never reaches disk, findByNormalizedUsername / findById return frozen copies, and insertUser does the duplicate check and the insert inside one in-process promise-queue mutex (single runExclusive queue, also exported) so concurrent callers serialize; persistence is write-to-users.json.tmp + fsync + renameSync (+ best-effort directory fsync), with in-memory rollback if the write fails and startup failure (never silent data loss) if users.json is corrupt. New src/store/secret-store.js: reads DATA_DIR/signing-secret on startup, otherwise generates 32 crypto.randomBytes, writes with flag wx and mode 0o600 (chmod as well), fsyncs, keeps the bytes in memory, supports restart reuse (byte-identical), only exposes defensive copies and never logs the value. New src/store/index.js: initializeStores() builds config via src/config.js, creates the stores and loads them, exposing getPersistenceStore/getSecretStore/getSigningSecret/getDataDir for the later register/login/token handlers. src/server.js now defaults its initialize hook to initializeStores(), so DATA_DIR is created, users.json loaded and the signing secret loaded/generated before the port is bound (start() still awaits initialize first and re-runs it after stop()); the store accessors are re-exported from server.js. Evidence: added test/store.test.js with 7 tests, every one named with the [AC-04] marker (recursive DATA_DIR creation + load, exact record fields with no plaintext password in any encoding anywhere under DATA_DIR, mutex serialization with 1 winner and 8 same-username contenders plus 20 concurrent distinct inserts, atomic write with no leftover .tmp and a stale truncated .tmp ignored, 32-byte secret with mode 0600 reused across restart, server initialize hook before listen plus restart persistence through the real start()/stop(), and startup-log hygiene). All 7 new [AC-04] tests pass; the pre-existing [AC-04] secret test in test/persistence.test.js now passes as well. lint, typecheck and build all exit 0. Note: the generic preamble mentions schema/migration files, but the deliverable paths named by this task (src/store/*.js, src/server.js) were accepted by the write policy, and the DATABASE spec for this slice is a JSON document under DATA_DIR (no SQL migrations), so no migration files were needed or produced.
